description: How Excel moves the references formula text makes when rows or columns of a sheet are inserted or deleted. Each case is a fresh workbook of sheets S1, S2 and S3: formulas, defined names and a data validation authored over COM, the edit made over COM, and every formula read back through Range.Formula (a defined name through Names.Item().RefersTo, a validation through Validation.Formula1) before and after. An insert moves every reference at or after it, absolute or not; a delete turns what it takes into #REF!, keeping the sheet prefix; whole columns ignore a row splice; a 3-D span and an INDIRECT string do not move; a single reference pushed past the last row is #REF! while a range bottom already there stays.
probe: a one-off COM script: Workbooks.Add, formulas via Range.Formula, Names.Add, Validation.Add, then Rows()/Columns() Insert or Delete
openClass: headless COM (DisplayAlerts off), a workbook created in the session, never saved

insert-rows.note: S1!D6 is empty before and after: D4 (=A4+A3) sits above the insert, so no cell lands on D6. dv:S1!F22 is the validation authored on F20 (=$A$5:$A$9), read where the insert moved it.

last-row.note: S1!D3 held =SUM(A1:A1048576), which Excel stores as =SUM(A:A); the insert at row 3 moved the cell itself to D4, so D3 reads empty after.
